purpose: Formal isolated-vs-schemata performance measurement for ROR schemata scoring, gating the first official performance claim after production enablement (SchemataLowererRegistry.builtIn).

scoutPhase.finding: Wall-proxy time (build+test seconds) increased monotonically with worker count for both modes and both projects on the public macOS runner (contention, not parallelism gain). swift-syntax at workers=4 additionally produced 4 isolated/schemata outcome disagreements out of 33 MutationIDs (verifiedTimeout/flaky on the isolated side vs survived/killedByAssertion on the schemata side) -- consistent with runner resource contention causing spurious isolated-side timeouts at that worker count, not a schemata-verification defect (0 disagreements at workers=2 and workers=3 for the same project). workers=2 selected for the formal run: fastest and disagreement-free for both projects.

officialClaim: Under these fixed conditions (same commit f2d5006, same MutationIDs, same workers=2, 5 repetitions, cold runs on GitHub-hosted macOS runners), ROR schemata scoring is measurably faster than isolated execution with zero correctness disagreement: +3.3% wall-time improvement on swift-numerics/IntegerUtilities, +8.1% on swift-syntax small-files. The effect is real but modest and should not be overstated -- both projects still fall back a large share of mutations to isolated execution within the schemata run (fallbackCount > effectiveCount in both corpora), which caps the achievable gain until more operators gain schemata lowerers.
